resolutions.what_changed: One regex on the shared parser, so both conjuncts move together: `(?mi)^[ \t]*(?:COPY|ADD)\s+`. Line continuations are joined first (`re.sub(r"\\\n[ \t]*", " ", text)`) — a sixth final-stage spelling found while fixing rather than reported: `COPY \` + newline + `  . /app/` was green too.
resolutions.watched_red: All eight reviewer spellings were added as self-test rows and watched RED against the unfixed parser BEFORE the regex changed: five `_not_caught` rows in the final stage (`copy . /app/`, `Copy . /app/`, `add . /app/`, ` COPY . /app/`, tab-indented) plus the continuation row, and two `_falsely_red` rows in the derive stage (`copy . /ctx`, ` COPY . /ctx`, each reporting `derive_stage_never_copies_the_context` with `copies: null`).
resolutions.why_it_mattered: A line the parser failed to match contributed no source, so the allowlist could not refuse it: default-red for lines it parsed, default-GREEN for every line it did not. Same fail-open-and-fail-closed signature that retired the denylist a round earlier, one layer down.

resolutions.what_changed: The absent row is added (`COPY . /ctx` -> `COPY src /ctx\nCOPY . /ctx`, must stay clean), and the count is no longer retyped anywhere: `_BUILD_SHA_SELF_TEST_ROWS = 20` is read back against the loop's own length, so a document and the list cannot disagree again. Twenty = 13 rows that must be red on a named conjunct + 6 that must stay clean + the vacuity guard.
resolutions.watched_red: Against a first-match-only read of the same parser (the pre-round-2 behaviour the row exists to guard): `{'mutation_derive-stage-copies-the-context-second_falsely_red': {'wrong': {'derive_stage_never_copies_the_context': {'context': '/ctx', 'copies': ['src'], ...}}}}`. Both documents that said ELEVEN are corrected — the case's ceiling (8) and pr67-r2-resolution.json.

condition_1_parser_surface_under_execute.detail: The parser's own surface is now eight of the twenty rows (case: lowercase/mixed/lowercase-ADD; whitespace: leading space, leading tab; continuation; plus the two derive-stage over-fire rows). The vacuity guard is itself a row, because it was the one piece of the exercise set nothing exercised: an absent mutation must report exactly `mutation_vacuity-guard_is_vacuous`, and the check reddens if it reports anything else. Demonstrated standalone: `_build_sha_mutation_row(orig, 'demo', 'COPY __absent__ /x', 'y', None)` -> `{'mutation_demo_is_vacuous': "'COPY __absent__ /x' is not in the Dockerfile"}`.

run_mount_bypass.fail_closed_neighbours: CORRECTED at round 4 (PR #67 R14): what this said was 'ARG-substituted source, heredoc COPY, and a lowercase FROM were probed in the same pass; all three are red'. Re-run and observed: the ARG-substituted source and the heredoc COPY are red. The FROM claim was wrong -- the probe that ran lowercased BOTH `FROM` lines (which does report `single_stage`) and the sentence generalised it. Lowercasing only the DERIVE stage's `FROM` raises an uncaught `ValueError: max() iterable argument is empty`, which the runner reports as a case ERROR: loud, so the gate stops, but the named conjunct never reports. Separately, `arg ZEABUR_GIT_COMMIT_SHA=""` in lowercase passes GREEN -- that regex fails open (R13). Neither is fixed in code; both are named in the case's ceiling (4).
run_mount_bypass.recorded_in: ADR-034 section 'What the `.git`-in-the-context tradeoff costs, and what the guard is worth' (structural: admitting `.git` to the context is what makes any context-reading instruction able to carry it, so this is a property of the tradeoff), the case's ceiling (9), and debt M44-P1-D8 with the probe verbatim and the CI cost note.
run_mount_bypass.framing: The guarantee is stated as 'an accidental context copy is caught', NOT '`.git` cannot reach the image'. ADR-034 gives both sentences and says which one is true.
